title: Microscopic exceptional points in the post-selected open Jaynes--Cummings model
abstract: Phenomenological non-Hermitian Hamiltonians track selected signatures of complex reservoir dynamics, while post-selected no-jump effective Hamiltonians derived from microscopic open-system theory reveal the underlying system--reservoir physics. We derive such a Hamiltonian for the open Jaynes--Cummings model using a Moore--Penrose normalized $\mathrm{su}(2)$ representation that removes the vacuum-sector singularity and diagonalizes the full Hamiltonian by one operator rotation. Starting from a zero-temperature bosonic reservoir, we obtain a Gorini--Kossakowski--Sudarshan--Lindblad master equation under the Born--Markov approximation with full Bohr-frequency resolution. We use partial Bohr-frequency resolution to build a consistent post-selected no-jump Hamiltonian near exceptional points, where decay rates become comparable to Rabi frequencies and remove the scale separation behind full resolution. The normalized $\mathrm{su}(2)$ form of the resulting non-Hermitian Jaynes--Cummings Hamiltonian reveals the effects of Lamb-shifted detuning, diagonal loss imbalance, and reservoir-modified coupling. Our microscopic exceptional-point analysis recovers the experimentally reported single-excitation exceptional point for unequal independent losses and identifies regimes absent from the standard phenomenological model; for example, equal correlated losses with orthogonal channel phase produce a second-order exceptional point at the same loss-to-coupling ratio in every excitation sector.
summary: The paper develops a detailed microscopic theory to analyze exceptional points in the open Jaynes–Cummings model. By using advanced techniques like partial Bohr-frequency resolution, it derives an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian that accurately captures system-reservoir interactions. The key contribution is identifying novel EP regimes beyond standard phenomenological models, which has implications for engineering quantum devices.
main_problem: To derive a microscopic, post-selected no-jump effective Hamiltonian for the open Jaynes–Cummings model and analyze its exceptional point (EP) physics in regimes where decay rates are comparable to Rabi frequencies.
main_result: The analysis recovers known single-excitation EPs but also identifies new regimes, such as a second-order EP occurring in every excitation sector under equal correlated losses with orthogonal channel phase.
method: The authors use partial Bohr-frequency resolution on the Born-Markov master equation to construct a non-Hermitian effective Hamiltonian, which is then analyzed using $	ext{su}(2)$ algebra techniques.
model_or_system: The system is the open Jaynes–Cummings model (coupling a bosonic mode to a two-level system) coupled to a zero-temperature bosonic reservoir. The dynamics are described by deriving an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian from the full Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: Exceptional Points (EPs), absolute value of doublet relative conditioned eigenvalues $|\lambda_{N,\pm}|/(\hbar g)$, and spectral singularities.
important_parameters: Lamb-shifted detuning, diagonal loss imbalance, reservoir-modified coupling strength, and the ratio of losses to coupling constants.
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on the Born–Markov approximation and utilizes partial Bohr-frequency resolution near EPs.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the transition ladder for JC sectors using frequency-resolved decay operators. Figure 2 compares the absolute value of doublet relative conditioned eigenvalues across four different loss models (independent, correlated, etc.) for various excitation numbers N.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the microscopic framework by deriving the master equation and then employs partial Bohr-frequency resolution to construct the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. The core analysis involves calculating EPs using this derived Hamiltonian, comparing results across different loss models, and highlighting novel physical regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, microscopic foundation for analyzing spectral singularities (EPs) in open quantum systems relevant to cavity QED and circuit-QED platforms by correctly handling the transition between full and partial frequency resolution near critical points.
